equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (40% Fiber Link Global at FY2024 sale value 5,745 + other NCI 76 at book)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR note 24(b): NCI 1,573 of which 1,500 Fiber Link; FY2024 cash flow: net proceeds from partial disposal 5,745. H1 FY2026 NCI profit 233.

memo_aff_capitalisation.method: Company AFF capitalised at cost of equity (the yield-vehicle framing the market uses) - MEMO ONLY, not the house value
memo_aff_capitalisation.note: AFF x 1.02 / (CoE - 2%) / 7,581 units. The gap between this memo (HK$12-14) and the owner-FCF value is the price of believing AFF: it omits ~HK$3.1bn/yr of software additions, assumes cash tax stays at ~3% of EBIT, and is already after interest at today's HIBOR. The market price (6.8% trailing distribution yield) sits inside this memo range.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (equity CAGR is not usable as a growth proxy: the trust distributes 100% of AFF so book value is flat by construction)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges >30% from revenue (2.4%) and 3yr EPS (2.6%) CAGRs. Explained by the full-payout policy, not by value destruction; growth is anchored on revenue/EBITDA instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - PPE - intangibles) - SBC - lease payments: FY2020 4,143; FY2021 3,719; FY2022 4,272; FY2023 4,765; FY2024 5,338; FY2025 4,709. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (3.3%) is above the reported-FCF CAGR (2.3%) only because lease payments fell from 1,389 to 1,343 and SBC is trivial; it is NOT a sign of SBC discipline, and FY2024-25 OCF is flattered by trade-payables growth of 1,431 and 2,511. EPS 5yr CAGR is ~0% because FY2020 (0.70) was a high base.

scenario_narratives.base: HKT stays the defensive HK incumbent: revenue compounds ~2.5% (enterprise/AI solutions +8% and 2500M+ fibre ARPU uplift offset exchange-line decline of 4-5%/yr and mobile price competition), EBITDA margin drifts to 38.7%, total reinvestment (PPE + software + spectrum + CAC + fulfilment) stays at ~20% of revenue after a 22% FY2026 DCI-build peak, and cash tax normalises from 3% to 14% of EBIT as deferred assessments catch up. Owner FCF grows ~2-3%/yr off a ~HK$4.9bn FY2026 base, well below the HK$6.2bn AFF the distribution is set on; the model takes no view on when the Board resets the payout, only that the cash distributed in excess of owner FCF is borrowed and therefore already in net debt.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI narrative delivers: the 3.2Tbps DCI superhighway and PCCW Global's hyperscaler interconnect business turn enterprise growth into group growth of 3-4% for a decade, bundling (3+ product customers +20%) lifts the EBITDA margin to 39.5%, the DCI build is genuinely customer-pre-funded so reinvestment falls to 19% of revenue with a 10% working-capital capture on growth, cash tax settles at 12% on continuing capex allowances, and a 20x exit at 2.5% terminal growth reflects a scarce HK infrastructure yield asset. Even here owner FCF only reaches the current AFF level late in the decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: Competition and capex intensity bite together: China Mobile HK and HKBN price pressure plus exchange-line erosion hold revenue growth to ~1%, product-sales mix and content costs (Premier League to 2031, World Cup) pin the margin at 37%, software/spectrum/DCI reinvestment stays at 21%+ of revenue, cash tax normalises fully to 16.5%, and a 15x exit at 1.5% growth. Owner FCF stalls around HK$4bn against a HK$6bn+ distribution, forcing either continued debt funding until the Baa2/BBB rating is at risk or a distribution reset - the latter removes the yield support that holds the price today.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value HKT on the cash the consolidated cash flow statement actually generates for unit-holders after every recurring reinvestment line (PPE, software and spectrum intangibles, customer acquisition and fulfilment costs, lease payments) and after cash tax normalises - not on the company's Adjusted Funds Flow, which omits ~HK$3bn/yr of software additions and is the basis of a distribution that has been partly debt-funded for years. Leverage (HK$46.6bn net debt incl. PCCW and NCI funding balances) and the Fiber Link 40% NCI (at its 2024 sale value) are deducted once each in the bridge; leases are charged in the flows and excluded from debt; risk is carried in three scenario paths and their weights at a single HKD WACC of 6.5%. The AFF-at-cost-of-equity memo (HK$12-14) is reported so the reader can see exactly what the market is paying for.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex definition: if a material part of the HK$3.1bn/yr software additions is customer-funded or non-recurring (DCI anchor prepayments), capex_pct is 2-3pp too high and value is understated by roughly HK$1.5-2.5 per unit; the FY2026 annual report's intangibles note and contract-liability movement are the evidence to watch.
Cash tax ramp: the 14% mature cash rate may overstate tax if HK capex allowances continue to defer indefinitely at today's ~3%; each 5pp of cash tax rate is worth ~HK$0.5-0.6 per unit.
WACC: at 6.5% the 18x cap binds; a buyer accepting 5.5% (yield-vehicle pricing) adds ~HK$2 per unit, which is why the sensitivity grid is shown.
Payout policy: a distribution reset would likely de-rate the units toward the owner-FCF value; its absence keeps the price anchored to the AFF yield and the gap is funded by debt.

Working capital: FY2024-25 OCF was flattered by +HK$3.9bn of trade-payables growth; a reversal would cut reported OCF without changing the model (wc_capture 0) but would make the payout gap visible sooner.
HIBOR/USD rates: ~HK$46bn of (partly USD) debt makes levered cash flow sensitive to rates; this sits in the discount rate and net debt rather than the unlevered flows.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 11.24-13.58
data_sources.financials: 6823.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2017-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026 interim) from core_metrics; FY2025 Annual Report (AFF table p.50-51, cash flow statement p.102, note 19 intangibles, note 24(b) NCI, note 34(a) OCF reconciliation); H1 FY2026 Interim Report (balance sheet 30 Jun 2026, AFF table, note 6 diluted units)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR note 34(a) OCF reconciliation, 'Share-based compensation expenses' HK$42m (2024: 34). No equity-award cash taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). HK$23m of units bought for the award schemes in FY2025 is recorded as buyback_cash.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average 7,580.4m Share Stapled Units for H1 FY2026 (interim report note 6, units in issue ~7,581m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged; the award schemes are funded by on-market unit purchases (HK$23m FY2025).
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026 interim balance sheet: short-term borrowings 7,721 + long-term borrowings 40,330 = 48,051 (company 'gross debt' definition), PLUS amount due to a fellow subsidiary 1,519 (PCCW group funding balance, moved through financing activities) and amount due to a non-controlling interest 305 (NCI shareholder loan to Fiber Link) = total_debt 49,875. Cash 2,747 + short-term deposits 480 = 3,227 (restricted cash 177 excluded). Lease liabilities (924 + 1,610 = 2,534) are EXCLUDED from net debt because lease payments are charged inside the flows (treatment B). Carrier licence fee liabilities (3,729) excluded: licence payments are inside capex_pct. Net debt has risen 41,306 (Dec-24) -> 44,575 (Dec-25) -> 48,051 (Jun-26) on the company definition.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD flows discounted at an HKD-built rate. Risk-free 3.4% (10y HK Exchange Fund Note, Oct-2026, tracking UST under the peg), ERP 6.0%, unlevered telco beta 0.5 relevered at D/E 0.51 (net debt 46.6bn vs market cap 91bn) -> 0.75, cost of equity 7.9%. Pre-tax cost of debt 3.8% (net finance costs 1,720 on ~45bn average gross debt), 3.2% after 16.5% HK profits tax. Weights 66% equity / 34% debt at market -> 6.3%, rounded to 6.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: operating risk (competition, capex intensity, payout sustainability) is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease payment (principal + interest, 'Payment for lease liabilities (including interest)' in financing: FY2025 1,343, FY2024 1,412, FY2023 1,430, FY2022 1,389, FY2021 1,624, FY2020 1,590) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (3.67% of FY2025 revenue). Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (5,837 - 1,245 = 4,592 = 12.6% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in the cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at HK$5,821m. The NCI is almost entirely the 40% of Fiber Link Global Limited (the 'Passive Netco') sold to a third party in FY2024 for HK$5,745m net proceeds (FY2024 cash flow statement); NCI profit share was HK$464m in FY2025 and HK$233m in H1 FY2026 (~8% of group profit), so the HK$1,576m book value would understate the leakage. Deduction = 5,745 (transaction value of the Fiber Link 40%) + 76 (other NCI at book). FY0 check: 2025 NOPAT on the component build (~8,030) less net finance costs (1,720) and the 464 NCI share lands near attributable profit 5,286 within tax-timing noise.
inputs.capex_definition: capex_pct_path is TOTAL reinvestment, not the company's AFF 'capital expenditures' line: PPE purchases 1,977 + intangible additions 3,557 (software 3,074 + carrier licences 791 per note 19, net of accruals) + customer acquisition costs 1,286 + fulfilment costs 687 (both paid through operating assets in OCF) = 7,507 = 20.5% of FY2025 revenue (FY2024: 6,970 = 20.1%). The AFF definition counts only PPE, CAC/licence fees, fulfilment and ROU payments (5,819) and omits the ~HK$3.1bn/yr of software additions, which have grown from 1.2bn (FY2017) to 3.6bn (FY2025) and are plainly recurring. D&A (ex-ROU) includes the matching amortisation of intangibles 1,936, CAC 1,228 and fulfilment 486, so the cash is charged once (capex) and the tax shield once (D&A).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table: non-US operating company with leases, NCI and high leverage -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). HKT is an operating telco, not an IAS-40 property trust, so the REIT/AFFO row does not apply; its stapled-trust wrapper and 100%-of-AFF payout change who receives the cash, not what the cash flow statement means (OCF is pre-interest with finance costs and lease payments in financing). AFF capitalisation at cost of equity is reported as a MEMO cross-check (memo_aff_capitalisation), not the house value. KEY FINDING: AFF (6,199) is not owner FCF. On the cash flow statement, OCF 11,628 - PPE 1,977 - intangibles 3,557 - lease payments 1,343 = 4,751 unlevered post-lease FCF; after finance costs paid 1,610 that is ~3,140 of levered FCF against 6,037 of distributions + 254 NCI dividends. The ~HK$2.5-3bn/yr shortfall has been funded by borrowings (net debt +3.3bn in FY2025, +3.5bn in H1 FY2026), the FY2024 Fiber Link stake sale (5,745) and trade-payables growth (+1,431 FY2024, +2,511 FY2025 inside OCF). Cash tax is also abnormally low (230 paid vs 904 expense; deferred assessments per note 34(a) footnote) and H1 FY2026 tax paid jumped to 445 from 196, so cash_tax_rate_path ramps from 8% of EBIT to 14%. last_fcf (6,052) = reported_fcf (OCF - PPE - intangibles, 6,094) - sbc 42 - interest_income 0; interest income (48, 37 received) is not stripped because net debt is 46.6bn (no net cash). The lease charge (1,343) is applied through lease_cost_pct_path in the component build, so the FY0 owner FCF the engine reproduces is ~4,700-5,100 (ex working capital), below last_fcf. Price is the 23-Oct-2026 HKEX regular close, not an after-hours print. SBC is immaterial (0.12% of revenue) so house and street bases nearly coincide; band_position is reported but is a narrow band.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +6%: H1 FY2026 revenue +8% was mobile-product-sales led (low margin); H2 FY2025 is a high base. Then 2.5-3% (5yr revenue CAGR 2.45%, enterprise +8% offset by exchange-line decline of 4-5%/yr), fading to 2% HK nominal growth.
base.margin_note: FY2025 EBITDA margin 38.9% (post-IFRS-16); H1 FY2026 35.2% vs 36.8% on product-sales mix, H2 seasonally ~41%. FY2026 EBITDA +3.5% -> 38.0%, recovering to 38.7% as 2500M+ fibre ARPU uplift and 5G mix improve, capped by five-operator competition.
base.capex_note: FY2026 22%: H1 FY2026 investing outflow 3,664 vs 3,037 (+20%) on the DCI/AI-superhighway and software build; eases to 20% (FY2024-25 average 20.3%) as the first DCI phase completes end-2026.
base.tax_note: Cash tax 2.8% of EBIT in FY2025 on deferred HK assessments and capex allowances; H1 FY2026 paid 445 vs 196. Ramps to 14% (below the 16.5% statutory rate because continuing capex allowances defer a residual portion in perpetuity).
base.terminal_note: Cap 18x owner FCF binds below Gordon (22.7x at 6.5%/2%); 18x is a 5.6% unlevered FCF yield, the multiple a regulated-utility-like buyer pays for a mature HK telco.

entry_price.note: House 15% hurdle applied for comparability. For a 6.5%-WACC yield vehicle this will sit far below intrinsic value; the required_return_table is the more useful reading of what return today's price implies.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the 100%-of-AFF distribution exceeds levered cash-flow-statement FCF by ~HK$2.5-3bn/yr and is being funded by rising debt (company-definition net debt +HK$6.7bn in 18 months) and payables growth, on a 37%-of-assets debt load; that is a structural coverage problem, not a cyclical one. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (AI DCI monetisation at scale, capex intensity falling while the build is still ramping, margin expansion in a five-operator market, and a low cash tax rate persisting). Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is HK$0.14 wide (SBC 0.12% of revenue, an effectively SBC-zero market); the computed band position (~5100%) is a degenerate reading and is reported as null. The price sits ~48 band-widths above both bases: SBC accounting explains none of the gap to the market, which is the AFF-vs-owner-FCF definitional gap described in inputs.notes.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
